reason: Seawater can enter the seafloor through open fractures, starting the circulation loop.
expectation: Seawater will flow down into the fractured rock.

effect: Seawater has entered the crust, so the next step is to heat it.
reaction: The circulation route is taking shape as expected.
reason: Water entering the crust can be heated by the rock beneath the seafloor.
expectation: The circulating seawater will heat up underground.

effect: The seawater is now heated under pressure inside the crust; it needs a route back to the sea.
reaction: The role of pressure in keeping the hot fluid underground is interesting.
reason: Inspecting the heated water will clarify how it can rise or react with the rock.
expectation: The compatibility list should reveal the next stage of the circulation loop.

alternatives.reason: Fractures might also provide a return route, but I don't yet know whether they are the next step.

effect: The heated water has reacted with buried rock and now carries dissolved material; the circulation still needs to return it to the sea.
reaction: The distinction between heating the water and exchanging material with rock is useful.
reason: The hydrothermal fluid needs a path back through the fractured seafloor, so I’ll try the open fractures.
expectation: The fluid will rise through the fractures toward the sea.

effect: The mineral-bearing fluid is rising through fractures and can now return to the sea.
reaction: The separate entry and return routes make the circulation loop clearer.
reason: The returning fluid should emerge into the surrounding seawater, where cooling may also form a deposit.
expectation: The hot fluid will enter the sea and mix with cooler seawater.

effect: Mixing with cooler seawater caused minerals to precipitate at a vent; I still need to complete both goals.
reaction: The change from dissolved material to solid minerals makes the deposit process clearer.
reason: Inspecting the precipitating minerals should reveal how to build the vent deposit.
expectation: The compatibility list will show what can turn the precipitating minerals into a deposit.

effect: Precipitated minerals have built a deposit around the outlet, completing that goal; returning heated water to the sea remains.
reaction: The modest deposit is a useful contrast to assuming every vent forms a tall chimney.
reason: Inspecting the returning fluid should reveal how to complete the circulation loop.
expectation: The compatibility list will show a way for the heated fluid to return to the sea.

effect: The returning fluid formed a hydrothermal plume, completing the circulation loop and the remaining goal.
reaction: The clarification that the visible plume is suspended mineral material, not smoke, was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the heated water’s reaction with rock through to mineral precipitation made the circulation and deposit formation understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final inspection felt less direct than combining the returning fluid with the sea, though it completed the goal automatically.

surprise.text: Mixing precipitated minerals separately from the plume’s formation, and the plume was described as suspended mineral material rather than smoke.

arbitrary.text: Combining precipitating minerals with open fractures to build the deposit was not obvious to me before the inspection revealed it.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for the clear explanations of how water, heat and rock interact, especially the distinction between dissolved material and precipitated minerals.
